metadata.independence_statement: This actual child session did not author or edit this project or these items. Parent instructions designated independent screening. Canonical key was read for comparison; this was not a blind-key audit. No other auditor verdict was used as substantive authority.
metadata.scope: Existing 28 public canonical items selected from existing released bank. No private source text, Drive image/ZIP, or private drafts accessed. No canonical question, rule, hash, data/audits, registry, git, or release status modified.

distractor_archetypes: correct federal rule but wrong Massachusetts consequence
correct deadline belonging to a different pathway
correct rule applied to the wrong schedule
general rule that ignores an exception
style_profile.familiarity_goal: A new lawful MPJE item should feel familiar in decision structure without reproducing protected content.
prohibited_similarity_methods: copying or lightly paraphrasing protected question wording
transforming recalled or confidential exam content
using commercial question text without explicit permission

metadata.legal_currentness_limit: Official sources retrieved directly on 2026-11-05. eCFR explicitly published current text through 2026-11-03; no claim of unseen November 4-5 legal changes. metadata.methodology: Read all 28 full items and all explanations; directly retrieve official primary bodies, verify exact substantive text and source identity beyond HTTP status, preserve original bytes and SHA256. Compare current canonical/suggestion/site content and hashes. Review full-bank lexical nearest stems and all shared-rule neighbor stems, then distinguish genuinely different decisions. No protected similarity corpus used.

results.legal_analysis: No Schedule II refill exists; a printed refill notation does not create separate prescriptions. At ten days even a genuine shortage remainder would have exceeded 1306.13(a).
results.realism_analysis: The stem presents a patient/dispensing-record discrepancy but the keyed action and explanation treat the profile as conclusive. results.legal_analysis: A valid no-substitution direction requires the exact prescribed product. Ordinary interchange is conditional; §12D prioritizes an interchangeable abuse-deterrent product if one exists, otherwise less-expensive reasonably available interchangeable product. C says generally/when conditions met, so does not make an absolute contrary claim. 247 CMR 9.05(1) separately permits a documented, patient-accepted medical-emergency deviation when the brand is unavailable; 9.05(2) treats generic prescriptions with no specified manufacturer separately. Neither predicate is supplied by this stem, but the broad explanation should not be memorized as eliminating those exceptions.
results.realism_analysis: A and B repeat the identical controlling proposition; D patient erasure is implausible and E is generic caution. The selected-response task largely counts paraphrases of one rule instead of making distinct product-selection decisions.
